candidates.name: Hepatic Encephalopathy
support_spans: Patient presented with hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and recurrent pleural effusion.
Progressive deterioration led to increased encephalopathy with concurrent hypotension requiring critical care unit transfer.
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with hepatic encephalopathy and its progression suggest a liver-related condition.

candidates.name: Cirrhosis
support_spans: A 61-year-old woman with cirrhosis secondary to alcohol use disorder in remission.
Demonstrated micronodular cirrhosis with dense fibrosis, scattered simple cysts, and bile duct hamartomas
candidates.why: The patient has a history of cirrhosis and the liver explant histology confirms micronodular cirrhosis.

candidates.name: Hepatitis C
support_spans: Initial negative HCV antibody, later positive
HCV viral load: 4,510,319 copies/mL (Hospital Day 4)
candidates.why: The patient's seroconversion to HCV positive and high viral load suggest a hepatitis C infection.

candidates.why: The patient's history of alcohol use disorder suggests a possible mechanism for her liver disease.
